templates.title: AD over LDAPS fails after the domain controller certificate was renewed
templates.issue: Active Directory users cannot log in to vCenter. The identity source shows it cannot contact the LDAP server on port 636 after the domain controller certificate was renewed.
lines: {t} ERROR [IdentityManager] [tomcat-http--8] Failed to probe provider ldaps://dc01.lab.example:636 : Can't contact LDAP server
{t} ERROR [IdentityManager] [tomcat-http--9] Failed to probe provider ldaps://dc01.lab.example:636 : Can't contact LDAP server
{t} WARN  [LdapSslHandshake] Server SSL certificate verification failed: unable to find valid certification path to requested target
{t} ERROR [IdentityManager] Failed to authenticate user svc-admin@corp.example against provider corp.example: Can't contact LDAP server
templates.cause: The domain controller LDAPS certificate was renewed with a new issuer chain that vCenter does not yet trust; the TLS connection to the DC on 636 fails (nc to 636 timed out and openssl s_client showed the Sub-CA/Root-CA chain).
resolution: Test from the VCSA: nc -zv <dc-fqdn> 636, then openssl s_client -connect <dc-fqdn>:636 -showcerts to confirm the chain presented.
Import the Root CA and Sub/Issuing CA certificates into the vCenter trust store (VECS TRUSTED_ROOTS).
Remove and re-add the Active Directory over LDAPS identity source.
Restart VMware Identity Services (expect a brief authentication interruption).
No per-DC leaf certificate upload is needed; keep Root + Sub-CA trusted. Re-adding is only needed again if the issuing CA changes.

templates.title: Cannot add AD over LDAPS identity source: domain controller certificate is SHA-1 signed
templates.issue: Adding an Active Directory over LDAPS identity source fails with a certificate error. vCenter can reach the domain controller on port 636.
templates.match: SHA1|Signature does not match|not a trusted certificate
lines: {t} INFO  [LdapSslValidator] Attempting Server SSL certificate verification ... [SHA1 Fingerprint: AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF:00:11:22:33:44:55:66:77:88:99:AA:BB:CC:DD]
{t} ERROR [LdapSslValidator] Server SSL certificate verification failed ... not a trusted certificate
{t} ERROR [LdapSslValidator] java.security.SignatureException: Signature does not match.
templates.cause: The domain controller LDAPS endpoint presents a SHA-1 signed certificate/chain. vSphere 8.x disallows SHA-1 anywhere in the TLS chain (leaf, intermediate or root), so SSO rejects the certificate while adding the identity source.
resolution: Reissue the DC LDAPS certificate from the CA with SHA-256 (SHA-2) or stronger, EKU Server Authentication (1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.1), and SAN = the DC FQDN that vCenter will use.
Export the leaf and any intermediate CA certificates in Base-64.

In vCenter: Administration > Single Sign-On > Configuration > Identity Sources - remove any existing LDAPS source tied to the old certificate, then add it again using the FQDN (not the IP) and import the new leaf + intermediates.
If trust problems persist, diagnose the vCenter trust/lookup store with lsdoctor in report mode first and apply fixes only if flagged.
If several DCs are configured, each must present a valid SHA-2 certificate with a matching SAN.

templates.title: Expired issuing certificate in the VECS machine certificate store
templates.issue: One of the issuing certificates is reported as expired. The customer asks whether the expired root certificate can be deleted.
templates.cause: The active Machine SSL certificate was valid; the expired item was a stale/expired CSR alias left in the MACHINE_SSL_CERT VECS store. No STS or solution-user certificate had expired.
resolution: List the VECS stores (TRUSTED_ROOTS, MACHINE_SSL_CERT) and check the STS signing certificate expiry to confirm the expired item is not in use.
Take a snapshot / backup before any certificate operation.
Remove the stale alias: vecs-cli entry delete --store MACHINE_SSL_CERT --alias <stale-alias>.
Restart vCenter services out of hours and verify service-control --status and UI/API access.

templates.issue: After a reboot the vSphere UI does not start. service-control --start vsphere-ui fails and the appliance root volume is full.

templates.cause: The appliance root logical volume (/dev/mapper/vg_root_0-lv_root_0, 48 GB) reached 100%, so services could not create temporary/PID/log files and failed to start (install.ciscommon.service.failstart).
resolution: Confirm with df -h / lsblk that the root LV is full.
Grow the VM virtual disk (here 48 GB -> 100 GB) in the ESXi/vSphere UI and reboot the appliance.
Verify service-control --status shows vsphere-ui, vpxd and dependents RUNNING and that / is back to roughly 60%.
Follow-up: extend the logical volume and filesystem (lvextend + resize2fs, or xfs_growfs for XFS) once the storage team enlarges the underlying disk.
Prevent recurrence: log rotation/retention for the VCSA and monitoring/alerting on / and /storage/log usage.

templates.title: Lifecycle Manager: compatibility-data sync fails after a database reset (verification service)
templates.issue: After resetting the Lifecycle Manager database, update sync works but compatibility-data sync fails with: unable to authenticate with the VMware verification service.
lines: {u} INFO  [qtp1297149880-18 INFO 'com.vmware.updatemanager.filedownload.FileDownloadServlet'] File /storage/updatemgr/patch-store-temp/SOFTWARE_SPEC_0a1b2c3d-4e5f-6071-8293-a4b5c6d7e8f9.json does not exist.

{t} error vmware-vum-server[85242] [Originator@6876 sub=Default] A general system error has occurred: unable to authenticate with the VMware verification service. Please try again and, if the problem persists, contact Broadcom support.
templates.cause: The SDDC Manager online depot entry in vCenter lost (or was re-created without) the ownerdata value sddc_manager_esx_depot after the Lifecycle Manager database reset, so the verification service rejects the sync.
resolution: Log in to the vCenter on which the Lifecycle Manager DB reset was performed.
Developer Center > API: GET the online depots (settings/depots/online) and note the depotId of the SDDC depot URL.
DELETE the existing SDDC depot entry using that depotId.
POST a new online depot with description "SDDC Manager Online Depot", enabled true, location = the SDDC Manager depot index URL, and ownerdata "sddc_manager_esx_depot".
GET again to verify the ownerdata field is present, then retry the sync.
templates.notes: The case cited no KB; the fix came from engineering and is documented in the case.

templates.title: vpxd will not start after removing vCenter HA; lockdown mode and NIC1 errors during HA redeploy
templates.issue: After removing vCenter HA and rebooting, vCenter does not come back. Afterwards, vSphere HA agent install and vCenter HA redeploy fail.
lines: {t} error vpxd[05993] [Originator@6876 sub=Default] Failed to parse configuration file /etc/vmware-vpx/vpxd.cfg: unexpected element (leftover vCenter HA block)
{t} error vmon Service vpxd failed to start; health check failed
{t} error hostd[2099] [Originator@6876 sub=Default] Access denied. Failed to configure VIM account. Operation breaks lockdown mode
{t} error vpxd[05993] [Originator@6876 sub=Default opID=op-300] vCenter HA network configuration failed: NIC1 not reachable
templates.cause: Primary: an incomplete vCenter HA (vCHA) removal left malformed configuration blocks in /etc/vmware-vpx/vpxd.cfg that stopped vpxd starting after the reboot. Secondary: ESXi lockdown mode without exception users blocked the HA agent; stale NIC1 bindings broke vCHA network detection; the witness VM was pinned to a host.
resolution: Remove all residual vCHA configuration (the malformed blocks in vpxd.cfg) and start services: service-control --start --all.
Lockdown mode: temporarily disable it on the hosts, configure vSphere HA, then re-enable it with the exception users (vpxuser, root); confirm port 8182 is open between hosts.
vCHA NIC1 detection: reassign the port group (temporary port group, then back to the correct one) to refresh the network stack.
Witness VM power-on blocked by "pinned to host": vMotion it away / clear the VM-host pinning and check DRS rules, then retry the vCHA deployment.

templates.title: vSphere Distributed Switch health check alerts after VLANs were removed from the physical switches
templates.issue: After removing about 20 VLANs on the physical switches, every host shows "vSphere Distributed Switch VLAN trunked status" and "MTU supported status" alerts. No traffic impact.
lines: {t} info vpxd[05993] [Originator@6876 sub=Default] vim.event.UplinkPortVlanUntrunkedEvent: VLAN 730 no longer trunked on uplink vmnic0
{t} warning vpxd[05993] [Originator@6876 sub=Default] DistributedVirtualSwitchHealthCheckEvent: Health status changed to RED
{t} warning hostd[2099] [Originator@6876 sub=Default] NetVDS: VLAN 730 health check probe failed on uplink vmnic1
{t} warning hostd[2099] [Originator@6876 sub=Default] DvsManager: VLAN trunk verification failed
{t} warning vpxa[2105] [Originator@6876 sub=Default] DVS health check: VLAN 283 flagged as unsupported for host esx-a01.lab.example
{t} cpu4:2097180)WARNING: NetVDS: MTU check failed for VLAN 285 (expected 9000, found 1500)
templates.cause: The vDS portgroups still reference VLANs (for example 730, 283, 285) that were removed from the physical switch trunks, so the health-check probes for VLAN trunking and MTU fail. The alerts are cosmetic: no vSAN or VM traffic impact.
resolution: Recommended: remove the unused VLAN-tagged portgroups from the vDS and make sure MTU is aligned between the vDS and the physical switches (9000 recommended for vSAN).
Alternative: disable the vDS health check: Networking > vDS > Configure > Health Check, untick "VLAN and MTU" and/or "Teaming and Failover".

templates.title: Two vCenters in Enhanced Linked Mode: vmdir READ_ONLY and failed pre-checks
templates.issue: VDT reports "[FAIL] VMdir Local State Check (Read)" and vdcadmintool shows vmdir in read-only state on one of two linked vCenters; an upgrade of the other fails at Stage 2.
lines: {t} Please use /usr/lib/vmware-vmdir/bin/vdcadmintool option 6 to confirm the state. Check /var/log/vmware/vmdird/vmdird-syslog.log to investigate.
{t} error vmdird t@139: Replication partner vc02.lab.example unreachable (Server down)
templates.cause: vmdir was left READ_ONLY. Findings in the case: on the second vCenter /etc/hosts mapped its FQDN to 127.0.0.1/::1 (intermittent LDAP failures); pre-checks showed an invalid trusted-root chain, duplicate registrations and an STS_INTERNAL_SSL_CERT mismatch; rsyslog "Too many open files" was seen separately.
resolution: Take offline snapshots of both vCenters first (avoid deleting large snapshots live: it consumed the call time).
Restore vmdird logging on both nodes, then review the directory topology (replication agreements) - a "Server down" entry was the first sign.
Set the vmdir state to NORMAL with vdcadmintool (option 5, Set vmdir state), then reboot both vCenters.
Verify replication: vdcrepadmin -f showpartnerstatus shows partners available = Yes; vmdir state NORMAL on both members.
Fix /etc/hosts so the vCenter FQDN does not resolve to loopback; run lsdoctor in report mode and apply fixes only if flagged; handle the rsyslog file-handle issue in a separate case.

templates.title: Hosts show Disconnected after a core network change; reconnect says "incorrect user name or password"
templates.issue: After moving a circuit to a new core router several hosts are Disconnected in vCenter. Restarting management agents does not help; reconnecting reports incorrect user name or password. Hosts are reachable by SSH and the Host Client.
lines: {t} warning vpxd[05993] [Originator@6876 sub=InvtHostCnx opID=op-77] Failed to connect to host esx-a02.lab.example: SSL Exception: handshake failure

Correct the network/routing/inspection change; the customer reported 95% of hosts reconnected immediately and the rest after minor tweaks - no vCenter DB work was needed.

Keep datastore capacity below about 85% full.
Check HBA driver/firmware parity against the VMware Compatibility Guide and review FC CRC counters.

templates.title: XCP-ng storage: SR almost full, coalesce stuck, then a VM will not start
templates.issue: A VM will not start after a backup job. The NFS storage repository is almost full and backups began failing earlier this week.
lines: {s} xcp01 SM: [21433] Insufficient space on SR 0a1b2c3d-1111-2222-3333-444455556666: SR_BACKEND_FAILURE_44
{s} xcp01 SMGC: [30112] Unable to coalesce 8f7e6d5c: no space to leaf-coalesce, the SR is full

templates.cause: Per the summaries: coalesce (which frees snapshot space) runs after a snapshot is deleted and can fail when the SR lacks free space, which keeps the SR full and lets VDI chains grow; SR_BACKEND_FAILURE_44 means insufficient space. The VM failing to start is the downstream symptom.

Rescan the SR to restart the garbage collector; shut the VMs down before rescanning for a better chance of offline coalesce (user report).
Keep roughly 30% free (XO docs summary); thin-provisioned local ext is more forgiving than thick LVM (Vates staff in a thread).
Then start the VM and review backup schedules that created the snapshots.

resolution: Run xoa check and journalctl -u xoa-updater -f -n 50 while reproducing.
Allow the proxy to pass xen-orchestra.com and nodejs.org untouched, or (lower security) set NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 in /etc/xo-appliance/env and restart xoa-updater.
